speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned a concerning rash and recent health changes, but I don't see any specific symptoms listed in your message. To begin my assessment, can you tell me when this rash first appeared and if you have had any fever or weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very rapid onset for the rash, especially with new symptoms like a cough and recent arthritis management. Did the rash appear in specific patterns like bands, or does it feel painful and burn rather than just itch? Also, have you noticed any shortness of breath or chest pain alongside the cough?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Has been diagnosed with arthritis. No other significant past medical history has been mentioned. Social history: The patient didn't provide any specific social history details during the initial consultation.

speaker: Patient
text: Reports a new onset cough along with skin and mucosal changes but denies fever, shortness of breath, joint pains, gastrointestinal symptoms, or recent illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a surprising conclusion from your previous doctor, as a rash and cough are not typical presentations for simple iron deficiency anemia. Given the rapid onset and the combination of skin and mucosal changes, could you describe exactly what the skin and mucosal changes look like? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Rash. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Feritin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme. The combination of a rapidly appearing rash, mucosal involvement, cough, and normal blood work rules out infection and anemia; this is likely an immune-mediated hypersensitivity reaction, possibly drug-induced.
